newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's new PM Majali picks streamlined cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's new PM Majali picks streamlined cabinet.

text.p: Jordan's new Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali on Wednesday picked a streamlined cabinet of technocrats to run the country up to elections due to be held by November.
The official Petra news agency published a list of 24 ministers, including Majali, approved by King Hussein after Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti tendered his resignation.
Majali, who also took over the defence portfolio, appointed Jordan's ambassador to the United States Fayez Tarawneh as foreign minister, a post which Kabariti had held.
He also appointed two deputy prime ministers, Abdullah Ensour and Jawad al-Anani.

Ensour, deputy prime minister in Kabariti's government, moves from higher education to administrative development. Anani, a former peace negotiator and top economic strategist, was also appointed minister of state for development and for cabinet affairs.
Planning Minister Rima Khalaf, Jordan's negotiator with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, kept her post, as did Minister for Religious Affairs Abdul-Salam al-Abbadi.
Nasser al-Lawzi moved from the transport ministry to Public Works and Housing.
Others, including the ministers of finance, trade and industry, energy and communications all left the cabinet.

Many of their replacements have served under previous governments and others were involved in peace talks with Israel, reflecting Majali's background as the leader of Jordan's negotiating team with Israel, who as prime minister in 1994 signed a peace treaty between the two countries.
